---
title: "Core Execution and CP-Math"
---

## Role

CP-Math should become Cellerator core execution.

It should not be a thin backend registry around SpMM. It should plan and execute biological operations over domain-aware structures and value planes.

Its responsibilities are:

- operation semantics;
- physical projection management;
- kernel and backend capability;
- analytical cost modeling;
- bounded empirical autotuning;
- prepared-operation lifetime;
- launch binding;
- workspace and stream integration;
- epilogue fusion;
- execution-order propagation;
- graph capture;
- training and transpose planning;
- distributed scheduling;
- instrumentation and plan persistence.

## Current v1 implementation

The current code already contains useful foundations:

- backend-neutral `spmm_request`;
- separate `spmm_bindings`;
- feature-order and sparse-structure identity;
- storage, compute, and accumulation fields;
- determinism, workspace, reuse, and epilogue policy;
- pointer-free `execution_plan`;
- backend capability queries;
- backend registry;
- structural candidate planner;
- device capabilities and fingerprint;
- `DeviceMathContext`;
- reusable workspace;
- physical CSR and BELL views;
- native tile adaptation;
- generic epilogue;
- CPU referee;
- focused tests.

Those pieces should be migrated, not discarded.

The current `PreparedExecution` ownership must not become the final core ABI. It copies the request and bindings, owns a device context and stream, and requires preparation to establish per-run state.

## Core object model

### Operation problem

A problem describes mathematics and logical identity.

```cpp
struct operation_problem {
    operation_kind operation;

    structure_handle structure;
    operation_shape shape;
    numeric_policy numeric;
    epilogue_descriptor epilogue;

    determinism_policy determinism;
};
```

It contains no live input or output pointers.

### Launch bindings

Bindings describe one execution.

```cpp
struct launch_bindings {
    value_plane sparse_values;

    biological_operand_view inputs[max_inputs];
    biological_operand_view outputs[max_outputs];

    scalar_parameter scalars[max_scalars];

    stream_context stream;
    transient_workspace_view workspace;
};
```

### Prepared operation

A prepared operation is reusable.

```cpp
using run_function = status (*)(
    const prepared_kernel_state&,
    const launch_bindings&,
    execution_session&);

struct prepared_operation {
    run_function run;

    backend_id backend;
    kernel_id kernel;

    structure_handle structure;
    projection_handle projection;

    persistent_kernel_state persistent;
    workspace_requirement transient_workspace;

    produced_order_contract output_order;
    plan_measurement_identity measurement;
};
```

Changing a dense input, output, bias, scalar, stream, or value generation should normally require only new bindings.

### Prepared program

A prepared program composes operations:

```cpp
struct prepared_program {
    span<prepared_operation> operations;
    span<order_transform_step> transforms;
    span<communication_step> communication;

    optional_graph_executable graph;
};
```

## Runtime ownership

One `CelleratorSession` owns device resources.

```cpp
class cellerator_session {
public:
    device_fleet devices;
    stream_pool streams;
    library_handle_pool handles;

    persistent_allocator persistent;
    stream_ordered_allocator transient;

    projection_cache projections;
    plan_cache plans;
    order_transform_cache transforms;
};
```

### Memory lifetimes

| Class | Lifetime | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Structure-persistent | Structure epoch | indices, masks, tile headers, hierarchy |
| Plan-persistent | Prepared operation | vendor preprocessing, graph-stable buffers |
| Launch-transient | One execution | reduction scratch, temporary crop, short pack |

Do not implement these as one globally mutable scratch allocation.

### Stream ownership

Streams belong to execution sessions or launch bindings.

A prepared operation may store stream-compatible descriptors. It does not own the only stream on which it can execute.

This permits:

- concurrent batches;
- overlapping communication;
- graph capture;
- pipeline execution;
- independent profiling;
- multi-GPU schedules.

### Library handles

cuBLAS, cuSPARSE, and other handles should be pooled or rebound by session and stream.

Repeated descriptor construction is allowed only in preparation, not steady-state execution.

## Operation contracts

The operation registry should grow from SpMM into biological primitives.

Initial core operation kinds should include:

- sparse or relation-weighted projection;
- row, feature, and module reduction;
- segmented reduction;
- graph or regulatory propagation;
- sparse gather and scatter;
- sequence-conditioned propagation;
- sparse-to-dense module projection;
- normalization and fused epilogue;
- sparse recurrent state update;
- top-k event or neighbor selection;
- Jacobian-vector and vector-Jacobian products;
- order transform;
- communication.

An operation describes semantics. Backends describe implementations.

## Numerical policy

Storage, multiplication, accumulation, scalar, bias, and output type are distinct.

```cpp
struct numeric_policy {
    dtype structure_value_storage;
    dtype dense_storage;
    dtype output_storage;

    dtype multiplication_type;
    dtype accumulation_type;
    dtype scalar_type;
    dtype bias_type;

    rounding_mode rounding;
    saturation_mode saturation;
};
```

Legal tuples are explicit.

Examples:

```text
f16 × f16 → f32 accumulation → f16 output
bf16 × bf16 → f32 accumulation → bf16 output
int8 × int8 → int32 accumulation → f16 output
fp8 × fp8 → f32 accumulation → bf16 output
```

A backend advertises supported tuples. Validation rejects incoherent combinations before planning.

## Planner architecture

The planner selects the fastest correct strategy.

### Planning timescales

#### During CellPack construction

Compute:

- semantic geometries;
- tile statistics;
- candidate dense fragments;
- partition summaries;
- projection capabilities;
- construction-cost estimates.

#### Once per device performance class

Calibrate primitive behavior:

- launch overhead;
- memory access patterns;
- mask decoding;
- dense RHS broadcast;
- shared-memory staging;
- MMA throughput;
- segmented reduction;
- atomics;
- projection conversion;
- communication topology.

A performance class groups devices with equivalent execution behavior. A physical UUID is not always the correct cache key.

#### Once per structure and operation signature

Enumerate legal candidates and estimate total cost.

#### Lazily on first use

Measure a bounded shortlist with representative bindings.

#### Periodically

Retune only when:

- kernel build identity changes;
- CUDA, driver, or library behavior changes;
- device performance class changes;
- workload shapes drift;
- reuse assumptions change materially.

### Candidate cost

For candidate \(k\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
C_k =&
\frac{
C_{\text{projection},k}
+
C_{\text{prepare},k}
+
C_{\text{static pack},k}
}{R} \\
&+
C_{\text{dynamic pack},k}
+
C_{\text{kernel},k}
+
C_{\text{epilogue},k}
+
C_{\text{order},k}
+
C_{\text{sync},k}
+
C_{\text{communication},k}
\end{aligned}
\]

where \(R\) is expected reuse.

Constraints include:

- correctness;
- numerical error;
- determinism;
- persistent memory;
- transient memory;
- graph capture;
- latency or throughput objective.

### Planner keys

Use separate keys.

```cpp
struct problem_key {
    operation_kind operation;
    operation_shape shape;
    numeric_policy numeric;
    epilogue_signature epilogue;
};

struct structure_key {
    structure_id structure;
    geometry_id geometry;
    projection_capabilities capabilities;
};

struct device_key {
    device_performance_class performance_class;
    runtime_build_id runtime;
    library_build_id libraries;
};

struct policy_key {
    reuse_class reuse;
    determinism_policy determinism;
    memory_budget_class memory;
    optimization_objective objective;
};
```

Pointers and current value generations are bindings, not plan keys.

A plan must still validate that the bound structure and value generation are compatible.

### Planning algorithm

```cpp
prepared_operation prepare(
    const operation_problem& problem,
    const prepare_policy& policy,
    cellerator_session& session) {

    auto candidates = enumerate_candidates(problem, session);

    reject_semantically_invalid(candidates);
    reject_numerically_invalid(candidates);
    reject_device_incompatible(candidates);
    reject_memory_incompatible(candidates);

    for (auto& candidate : candidates)
        candidate.predicted_cost =
            analytical_cost(candidate, policy, session);

    auto shortlist = select_top_k(candidates, policy.autotune_width);

    materialize_required_projections(shortlist, session);
    benchmark_complete_candidates(shortlist, policy, session);

    auto winner = choose_robust_winner(shortlist, policy);
    persist_measurement(winner, session);

    return instantiate(winner, session);
}
```

Benchmarking uses private outputs and the same epilogue, packing, and ordering required in production.

### Measurement persistence

Store:

- median;
- dispersion or tail;
- sample count;
- device performance class;
- kernel build identity;
- library version;
- structure statistics;
- complete cost components;
- numerical result;
- validity horizon.

Do not persist a winner without the evidence needed to invalidate it later.

## Physical projection management

A structure owns a projection catalog.

```cpp
struct projection_catalog {
    span<projection_descriptor> available;
    projection_builder_registry builders;
};
```

A projection may be:

- persisted;
- lazily built;
- cached;
- invalidated by a structure epoch;
- refreshed by a value generation when values are reordered.

Projection construction should be GPU-resident when a full-data transformation is required and the device path is faster.

## Kernel families

## `N = 1`

### High-sharing row-masked

Use the existing lane-per-row traversal when:

- descriptor masks are dense;
- rows share blocks;
- lane work is balanced;
- metadata per value is low.

### Low-sharing fallback

Use:

- compact row-to-record adjacency;
- one subwarp or warp per heavy row;
- row work queues;
- CSR or SELL fallback.

Do not make all 32 lanes walk descriptors that serve only one or two lanes.

## Small `N`

For \(N \in \{2,4,8\}\):

- retain a short register vector per row;
- pack dense RHS into execution feature order when reuse justifies it;
- broadcast feature vectors across participating rows;
- fuse bias and activation where profitable.

## Medium `N`

For roughly \(N=16\) to \(64\):

- assign several row tiles to one CTA;
- deduplicate active feature blocks;
- stage dense RHS slabs;
- share them across warps;
- accumulate row-by-channel register tiles;
- fuse epilogue;
- emit module-major dense state when appropriate.

On Volta, use cooperative loads and manual double buffering.

On Ampere and later, specialized kernels may use asynchronous global-to-shared transfers.

On Hopper and later, specialized implementations may use TMA, warp-group matrix operations, and producer-consumer warp roles.

## Dense fragments

Locally dense fragments may use MMA or WMMA.

The planner includes:

- expansion cost;
- zero-fill cost;
- reuse;
- output channel width;
- precision error;
- surrounding sparse work.

Tensor Core use is opportunistic, not a format mandate.

## Heavy tails

Long rows, hub genes, and irregular regions may require:

- dedicated multiwarp row kernels;
- separate work queues;
- segmented algorithms;
- conventional sparse fallbacks.

The compiler should identify them rather than forcing them through the common tile.

## Epilogue fusion

Candidate fused epilogues include:

- bias;
- activation;
- residual;
- gating;
- normalization;
- quantization;
- order-aware output placement.

Do not compile an unlimited combinatorial epilogue matrix. Maintain a small measured set and a generic fallback.

The planner must include the cost of a separate epilogue when fusion is unavailable.

## Sparse-to-dense learned projection

A central native kernel should consume biological tiles directly into module-local dense state.

```text
packed biological tile
+ execution-ordered learned weights
+ optional state gate
    ↓
module-local accumulation
+ bias
+ activation
+ normalization
    ↓
[cell tile][module][hidden channel]
```

This should be benchmarked against:

```text
native input
    → CSR conversion
    → generic SpMM
    → separate epilogue
    → output reorder
```

The complete path decides the winner.

## Training

Training requires explicit forward and transpose projections.

For:

\[
Y = A X
\]

the runtime may need:

\[
\nabla_X = A^\top \nabla_Y
\]

and:

\[
\nabla_A = \nabla_Y X^\top
\]

The structure should support:

- forward projection;
- transpose projection;
- logical edge identity;
- projection-local value mapping;
- fp32 master values;
- lower-precision execution values;
- gradient accumulation;
- optimizer update in execution order;
- value-generation refresh.

Do not rely on atomics over a forward-only row projection as the permanent backward design.

## CUDA Graphs

Graph replay is appropriate when:

- topology is fixed;
- addresses are stable;
- operation sequence repeats;
- launch overhead matters;
- communication schedule is stable.

Prepared programs should expose graph-capture compatibility and required stable buffers.

Do not place hidden allocation or stream ownership inside a prepared operation that prevents capture.

## Persistent kernels and work queues

Persistent CTAs may help when:

- there are many tiny tile classes;
- active modules vary strongly;
- work is heavy-tailed;
- a device-side queue avoids launch trains.

They may hurt when:

- occupancy is monopolized;
- other streams need resources;
- work is regular enough for ordinary kernels;
- queue traffic exceeds launch savings.

The planner selects them by measured workload.

## Baseplane producer capabilities

Baseplane may register producer implementations such as:

- sequence predicate to bit plane;
- sequence predicate to event stream;
- direct sequence predicate plus regulatory accumulation;
- interval join;
- compact sequence-derived relation construction.

The planner compares materialized and fused routes.

Baseplane does not need to expose its internal C++ classes to the planner. It exposes stable capabilities and device views.

## Vendor backends

Vendor libraries are first-class candidates.

Use cuSPARSE, cuBLAS, CUB, NCCL, CUTLASS-like paths, or future libraries when:

- semantics match;
- projection cost is acceptable;
- descriptor preparation is amortized;
- padding is safe;
- complete execution wins.

Do not prefer or reject vendor libraries by ideology.

## BELL safety rule

A BELL backend must either:

1. prove that logical and padded M and K are equal; or
2. own padded dense input and output buffers, zero fill, pack, crop, and their cost.

It must never pass a logical-sized buffer to an operation whose descriptor legally accesses padded dimensions.

Add adversarial tests for dimensions not divisible by every supported block size.

## Multi-GPU

The core planner may choose:

- cell or batch partitioning;
- module or feature partitioning;
- sequence-coordinate partitioning;
- hybrid partitioning;
- replication of small shared modules.

A prepared distributed program includes:

- local projections;
- boundary-edge sections;
- communication buffers in execution order;
- NCCL or peer steps;
- overlap schedule;
- output ownership.

Do not canonicalize before communication unless the remote consumer requires canonical order.

## Precision

Precision is selected by biological error and performance.

Possible classes include:

- bit and Boolean;
- 2, 4, or 8-bit categorical or quantized;
- int8;
- fp8;
- fp16;
- bf16;
- fp32;
- fp64 where necessary.

Different tiles or modules may use different precision classes, but the number of runtime classes should remain small enough to batch effectively.

Quantization parameters may be per:

- value plane;
- module;
- feature block;
- tile class.

The planner includes dequantization, scale access, and output error.

## CP-Math migration

### Preserve

- request validation concepts;
- feature-order identity;
- structure identity;
- pointer-free execution plan;
- backend capability;
- device fingerprint;
- referee;
- physical projection experiments;
- tests.

### Replace

- `PreparedExecution` as the public reusable execution object;
- per-prepared-operation device context ownership;
- single-allocation workspace semantics;
- structural-only planner selection;
- SpMM-only operation model;
- bindings frozen through preparation;
- incomplete mixed-precision contract.

### Integrate

- existing sparse runtimes;
- CellPack native consumers;
- CSR, SELL, Blocked-ELL, quantized, and vendor paths;
- Baseplane producer capabilities;
- distributed session ownership;
- graph and order planning.

## Success criterion

CP-Math is complete when a caller can provide:

- biological structures;
- changing value planes;
- an operation or program;
- a device and policy;

and receive the fastest validated execution strategy without manually deciding:

- format;
- feature order;
- row order;
- backend;
- padding;
- fusion;
- workspace;
- graph capture;
- communication.

The planner should make that decision with less overhead than the execution it improves.
